scenes.line1: What happens when a Kafka broker dies?
scenes.say: If a Kafka broker goes down, how does the system keep running smoothly? Who takes charge next?

scenes.label: Leader
scenes.sub: Each partition has one broker as its leader.
scenes.say: Every partition in Kafka has one broker acting as its leader, handling all reads and writes for that partition.
If a broker fails, Kafka quickly checks the in-sync replicas for each affected partition, elects a new leader, and keeps service running. Clients reconnect without manual steps.

left.title: Before failure
items: Partition zero led by Broker one

scenes.say: Picture this: partition zero is led by broker one, with broker three as a backup. If broker one fails, broker three steps up as the new leader.

scenes.question: What ensures failover works?
scenes.right: Setting the replication factor for enough in-sync replicas
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: just adding brokers isn't enough. You need to set the replication factor so there are enough in-sync replicas to handle failures.
